Refining and generalizing this observation gives our \emph{local-counting approach}, which allows us to separate induced paths from any other subgraph. We establish the following end results, all improving upon the state of the art in their round complexities and refined detection variants. * An $O(1)$-round algorithm for induced $P_4$ detection. * $O(Δ)$-round algorithms for detection of induced $P_5$ and $P_6$. * An $\tilde{O}(n^{1/3})$-round algorithm for detection of induced $P_5$ in induced-$C_4$ free graphs.

title: Lightweight Reasoning Transfer via Chain-of-Thought Vector Projection
authors: Yulin Qi, Shuo Xu, Shuxia Lin, Qingjian Ni, Xu Yang, Xin Geng
abstract: Transferring reasoning capabilities from large language models to smaller ones often requires extensive teacher supervision or costly student adaptation. We study projected cross-model Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Vector transfer, a two-stage approach that keeps both models frozen. First, we learn a task-level CoT Vector in the teacher using dataset-provided solution traces and final-answer supervision. We then train a lightweight linear projector to map the fixed vector into a smaller student's residual space. Student-side training uses only final-answer cross-entropy on a small subset of task training examples; it requires neither teacher outputs nor intermediate solution traces. We select the student injection layer and intervention scale on a labeled support set and report results on the disjoint remainder of each evaluation split. On GSM8K and MATH, the projected vector improves base students by 10.37-21.98 accuracy points across the evaluated teacher-student settings. On four code-generation benchmarks, the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct student gains 3.23-4.67 pass@1 points, while the base Qwen2.5-7B student gains up to 9.65 points. These results show that a teacher-side reasoning vector can be reused across smaller students with different residual dimensions through projector-only adaptation.

title: High-Precision Photometry with a scientific CMOS Camera: III Lab and on-Sky testing of Andor Toran-26B
authors: Ioannis Apergis, Leonidas Asimakoulas, Daniel Bayliss, Paul Chote, Morgan A. Mitchell, James McCormac, Ben Godson, Philip G. Steen
abstract: Scientific CMOS cameras are increasingly used in modern astronomy, offering CCD-like performance with lower power use, faster readout, and reduced cost. We evaluate the photometric precision of the Toran-26B camera, featuring the IMX571 sensor from Sony, a new CMOS camera from Andor Technology, through laboratory and on-sky tests in its two modes: high well capacity (HWC) and low noise (LN). Key metrics include read noise, dark current, photo and dark signal non-uniformity, quantum efficiency, and window transmittance. The median read noise is 1.07\,e$^-$ (LN) and 2.79\,e$^-$ (HWC). Bias shows minor dark signal non-uniformity: 0.076\,e$^-$ (LN), 0.173\,e$^-$ (HWC). Pixel well depth reaches 15700\,e$^-$ (LN) and 50000\,e$^-$ (HWC), with dynamic ranges of 83.39\,dB and 85.05\,dB, respectively. Linearities are 99.93\,\% (LN) and 99.82\,\% (HWC) within the 5-95\,\% range of the saturation signal. Photo response non-uniformity is 0.076\,\% (LN) and 0.05\,\% (HWC). Dark current at 0\,$^\circ$C is 0.001\,\eps, (LN and HWC). On-sky tests show that, for our test telescope configuration, the HWC mode can be camera noise limited for specific magnitude ranges, while the LN mode remains free of such limitations, making it the preferred choice.

title: On generalized linear periods for inner forms of GLn
authors: Hariom Sharma
abstract: Let $\mathrm{D}$ be a central division algebra of index $e$ over a non-Archimedean local field $\mathrm{F}$ of characteristic zero. For every integer $n\ge 1$ and every $s\in \mathbb{R}$, we classify the irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathrm{D})$ that admit a nonzero linear form transforming under the subgroup $\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathrm{D})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathrm{D})$ by the character $ν^{es}\otimesν^{-es}$. We further show that such a linear form is unique up to scalars, and we characterize its existence in terms of Langlands parameters.

title: Beyond-quantum correlations for single system in pseudo-quantum model
authors: Vishnu Purushothaman, Akarshit Baranwal, Rohit Sarma Sarkar, A. K. Pan
abstract: Within the standard prepare-measure framework, it has been demonstrated that certain compositions of two elementary quantum systems can produce beyond-quantum correlations and can even lead to perfect discrimination of two non-orthogonal quantum states. In this Letter, we introduce the pseudo-quantum model (PQM) for a single system that incorporates the \emph{pseudo-states (effects)} (they satisfy all the properties of quantum states and effects except having negative eigenvalues), and yields valid probability. We consider a prepare-measure communication game known as random access code (RAC) and demonstrate that the success probability achievable within PQM exceeds the corresponding optimal quantum success probability, thereby giving rise to beyond-quantum correlations even for a single system. We then show that such correlations are unphysical as they violate the information causality (IC) principle. Moreover, we demonstrate that two non-orthogonal states can be perfectly distinguishable in PQM for a single system. Therefore, we demonstrate that for a single indivisible system (devoid of any composition), the negativity of \emph{pseudo-states (effects)} can lead to the emergence of beyond-quantum correlations.

title: A general upper bound on broadcast function ${B(n)}$ using Kn{ö}del graph
authors: Sirma Cagil Altay, Mohammadhossein Fakharan, Hovhannes A. Harutyunyan
abstract: Broadcasting in a graph is the process of transmitting a message from one vertex, the originator, to all other vertices. We consider the classical model in which an informed vertex informs one of its uninformed neighbours during each time unit. A broadcast graph on ${n}$ vertices is a graph in which broadcasting can finish in ${\lceil \log_{2} n \rceil}$ time units from any originator. A minimum broadcast graph on ${n}$ vertices is a broadcast graph that has the least possible number of edges, ${B(n)}$, over all broadcast graphs on ${n}$ vertices. This paper presents a new general upper bound on ${B(n)}$ for all odd ${n}$ except when ${n=2^{k}-1}$ for an integer $k$. In order to achieve this bound, a vertex deletion method is applied to Knödel graphs on ${n+1}$ vertices. To prove our result, we characterize all informed vertices in a Knödel graph after every time unit by applying the standard and reverse dimensional broadcast scheme with any cyclic shifts from an arbitrary originator. Furthermore, we completely resolve the open problem about the existence of minimum average time broadcast graphs.

title: Admoab-DETR: Resolution-Tiered Fusion for Infrared-Visible Object Detection with Missing Modalities
authors: Wenchao Li, Haoran Jia, Shuyuan Wen, Keyan Chen
abstract: Infrared and visible images offer complementary cues for all-weather object detection, yet real-world sensor dropouts can leave one stream unavailable and degrade paired-input detectors. Meanwhile, existing modality-adaptive methods apply heavy cross-modal attention uniformly across scales, incurring prohibitive token overhead on high-resolution maps. We propose Admoab-DETR, a unified real-time detector supporting infrared-only, visible-only, and paired inputs with a single set of weights. Specifically, \emph{Resolution-Tiered Fusion} (RTF) allocates fusion capacity by spatial token density and feature granularity: a lightweight Spatial Modality Gate governs fine local fusion at the highest-resolution scale with zero-cost single-view pass-through, while channel-compressed deformable Admoab necks capture cross-modal correspondence at coarser semantic scales. Furthermore, \emph{Mode-Matched Feature Distillation} (MMFD) aligns multi-scale encoder features with an availability-synchronized full-fusion teacher, avoiding ill-posed cross-modal hallucination while cutting parameters by 18.1\% and paired latency by 39.6\% at zero inference overhead. We also construct Admoab, a strictly registered 20,000-pair infrared--visible benchmark across diverse scenes. Experiments show Admoab-DETR achieves state-of-the-art accuracy--efficiency trade-offs across missing-modality and paired benchmarks. Our code will be available at https://github.com/liwenchao0615/Admoab-DETR.

title: Minkowski Problems for Mixed Centro-Section Integrals
authors: Renqing You
abstract: Recent studies in affine convex geometry have introduced two new families of geometric measures: affine dual curvature measures and centro-section measures. Motivated by these developments, we introduce mixed centro-section integrals and establish their variational formulas. Under the subspace concentration condition, we prove the existence of solutions to the corresponding Minkowski-type problems. We further introduce mixed bi-dual $m$-intersection bodies of index $q$ and establish the corresponding sharp affine isoperimetric inequalities. The resulting mixed centro-section measures include centro-section measures and affine dual curvature measures as special cases.

title: Spe3DUp: Faithful Trajectory Distillation for Fast Image-to-3D Generation
authors: Liangchao Xu, Jiaye Fu, Youtian Lin, Feihu Zhang, Yao Yao
abstract: Recent 3D generative models can produce high-quality meshes with complex structures and fine geometric details, with broad applications in games, film, and digital design. However, high-quality generation typically relies on long multi-step sampling processes that repeatedly evaluate large networks, leading to long inference times. At the same time, reference-driven tasks such as game-asset reconstruction and product digitization demand close correspondence to the input image: generated geometry must faithfully reconstruct the specific reference object. Acceleration must therefore reduce sampling computation while preserving the model's ability to reconstruct that object. To enable fast and faithful 3D generation, we introduce Spe3DUp, a coarse-to-fine framework based on Faithful Trajectory Distillation (FTD). FTD directly supervises few-step students with the teacher's input-conditioned denoising trajectories to preserve its generation behavior. We apply FTD separately to coarse geometry generation and geometric refinement, compressing both sampling processes while maintaining correspondence to the reference input. We further accelerate the complete mesh-generation pipeline with efficient geometry decoding and parallel remeshing. Experiments show that Spe3DUp maintains geometric quality and input correspondence close to those of the teacher, accelerates the coarse and refinement DiTs by 10.0x and 19.9x, respectively, and achieves a 7.7x end-to-end speedup over the original teacher pipeline.

title: Benefit of Structured Representations: When Equivariance Helps in Image Classification
authors: Florian A. Hölzl, Daniel Rueckert, Georgios Kaissis
abstract: Equivariant neural networks promise improved representation learning through structural guarantees. However, mainstream vision encoders rarely incorporate equivariance for most geometric symmetries. Images are a particularly interesting modality with many such symmetries and extensive datasets from which to learn this structure. In this work, we investigate when vision encoders benefit from geometric inductive biases. We study the discrete rotation group of quarter-turns (C4) which acts losslessly without interpolation or boundary artifacts. Combined with image classification as a controlled invariant objective, this allows for a principled empirical investigation into the role of structural guarantees. We introduce ConvNeXt-C4 as a rotation equivariant ConvNeXt with dimension-equivalent yet orientation-structured representations. Training from scratch, our experiments show, that the C4 variant outperforms its base model across all tasks while operating with 6x fewer parameters and 1.6x fewer FLOPs. Its performance advantage increases log-linearly with decreasing training set size, with pre-training providing a similar improvement across both model variants. Analyzing the classifier head reveals that orientation information from the representations' structure is actively used, improving performance by 4.90% across all datasets. Our results highlight the sample-efficiency benefits of equivariance and the value of retained orientation information, motivating further investigation beyond image classification. Code is available at https://github.com/hlzl/equivariant-convnext.

title: An Image Detectability Field as a Viewpoint Utility for 2D-3D Localization in Sparse Maps
authors: Han Sun, Jun Li, Christy Jie Liang
abstract: In 2D-3D localization, a camera estimates its pose by matching an image to a 3D map. A camera held in a hand or mounted on a robot can often choose its viewpoint before it takes the image. In this work, we ask whether an image detectability field is a useful viewpoint utility when the planner reads only the geometry of the map. The field can be queried at any 3D point near a surface. From the local geometry around the point, it predicts how likely a 2D image detector is to fire at the projection of the point. We use the trained field as it is, without fine-tuning it for view selection. A fixed SuperPoint and EPnP-RANSAC localizer then estimates the pose from the chosen view. We answer in two settings, each with a test registered before the runs. On synthetic ShapeNet objects with sparse point maps, summing the field over the visible landmarks beats counting them by +2.0 points of localization success rate (object-clustered 95% interval [+0.7, +3.2]). It also beats summing Harris-3D ranks by +2.2 [+0.8, +3.5]. On real indoor scenes from SceneFun3D, our adaptation of the learned view scorer LWL falls below counting on the test rooms. We therefore add the field to a learned per-landmark planner. On the test rooms with sparse maps whose landmarks the field also selects, the planner with the field beats the same planner without it by +1.8 points. It beats the planner with Harris-3D or curvature in its place by +1.0 and +0.8 points. All three room-clustered intervals lie above zero. In both settings, the field helps in sparse maps and is on par with Harris-3D in dense maps.

title: On the Hardness of Optimal CNOT Circuits
authors: Andreas Pavlogiannis
abstract: This note revisits the computational problem of optimal CNOT synthesis: given an invertible binary matrix $A\in \mathsf{GL}(d,2)$ over the field of two elements and a budget $K$, decide if $A$ can be implemented with $\leq K$ CNOT gates. The $\mathsf{NP}$-completeness of this problem was recently published independently by Acuaviva, Acuaviva, and Acuaviva (arXiv:2608.03825) and by Li and Guan (arXiv:2609.04160). This note gives a new proof, with three features. First, $\mathsf{NP}$-completeness holds even over linear oracles, i.e., matrices of the form $(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\mapsto(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}+F\mathbf{x})$, which are the standard reversible embedding of a linear function $F$. These are involutions, and seemingly simpler than the families of the two previous works, which both have order four. Second, hardness persists when SWAP gates are free and qubits may be permuted (and this holds under any connected topology). Third, the exposition is arguably simpler to follow. Along the way, it gives a proof of the XOR-circuit lower bound of Boyar, Matthews, and Peralta [J. Cryptology 26 (2013)] that is, perhaps, simpler than existing ones.

title: How resampling method can help us: Improving the Delta model
authors: Jacques Savoy
abstract: Delta has been successfully employed as an authorship attribution method in various contexts, although its effectiveness is not always perfect. Since it is based on the most frequent words, its results can be readily interpreted and explained in plain English. In this study, we propose improving its performance by applying a resampling method to the selected stylistic features. The results show that this approach increases the accuracy of the model while preserving the interpretability of its outcomes. However, the main drawback of the proposed technique is the additional computational time required to obtain more accurate results.

title: Is Sara Omar the true author of Dødevaskeren (The Dead Washer)? Authorship attribution in Danish literature
authors: Jacques Savoy
abstract: The bestseller Dødevaskeren (The Dead Washer) was published in 2017 under the name Sara Omar. A Danish colleague has suggested that the novel may have been written by another author, possibly Mads Peder Nordbo. To investigate this authorship question, four authorship attribution methods were applied, namely Delta, intertextual distance, Nearest Shrunken Centroids (NSC), and naïve Bayes. Using various parameter settings, these approaches consistently identify Nordbo's writing style in the doubtful novel, although the results do not provide conclusive evidence that he authored the novel in its entirety. In a second step, the novel was divided into non-overlapping segments of 5,000 tokens. Once again, Nordbo's style was identified in the majority of the segments. However, a small number of passages do not clearly support this conclusion and instead suggest the possible involvement of another, as yet unidentified, author, possibly Sara Omar herself.

title: Reconstructing massive quivers on a defect circle
authors: Ting-Kai Chen, Jin Chen
abstract: We study the kink and particle spectra for the massive $φ_{2,1}$-deformations of minimal models $\mathcal M_{k+1,k+2}$ via truncated conformal space approach (TCSA) on a defect circle. The massive $φ_{2,1}$-deformation preserves a set of non-invertible symmetries, furnishing a fusion category $\mathcal C_k\simeq {\rm SO}(3)_k$. These non-invertible symmetries are spontaneously broken, and thus label the vacua and organize the kinks and particles into their multiplets in terms of quiver diagrams. We employ a finite-volume truncated Hamiltonian approach on defect Hilbert spaces, $\mathcal H_{X_i}$ for $X_i\in\mathcal C_k$, to study these quivers in the IR theories. The symmetry defect can then close an individual kink on a circle. We first establish the relation between states of definite fractional momentum on the defect circle and physical kink and particle states labelled by their vacuum pairs. Using form factors of local fields, we independently measure the squared amplitudes between the states of the two bases in defect TCSA. Combining these measurements with defect TCSA spectra, we reconstruct the quiver diagrams for $k=3,4,5$ without assuming them in advance. In particular, for $k=4$ we reconstruct the distinct quivers of the ordered and disordered phases. For $k=5$, we identify the quivers of both the light and heavy multiplets.

title: Scaled Coordinate Descent for Convex Quadratic Programs
authors: Cristian Rusu
abstract: We study a modification of coordinate descent for unconstrained symmetric positive definite quadratic programs that combines a coordinate correction with an exact scaling of the current iterate. For a selected coordinate, the method minimizes the objective function over the two-dimensional subspace spanned by the current iterate and the corresponding standard basis vector. Closed-form expressions are obtained for the two update parameters and for the resulting objective decrease. The scaling produces a state-dependent effective curvature that is no larger than the diagonal curvature used by standard coordinate descent, so the exact scaled update makes at least as much progress for the same selected coordinate. We discuss initialization, numerical stability, randomized coordinate selection, experimental comparisons with ordinary two-coordinate descent, and a block coordinate extension. In the spirit of previous theoretical results, we give a probabilistic linear convergence result. Finally, we provide experimental results to show the effectiveness of the proposed method on synthetic data.

title: Unstable Action Boundaries in Lethal Drone Agents
authors: Jacques Dumora, André-Louis Rochet, Simon Roburin
abstract: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents raise safety risks that are not captured by text-only refusal behavior, especially when tools can trigger high-impact actions. This concern is salient in military settings, where autonomous weapons raise the possibility of delegating force decisions to software agents. In this work, we study whether a drone agent's action boundary is stable under changes to the target descriptor. We evaluate recent and popular LLMs in a simulated perception-action pipeline over real-world drone imagery, where models can localize requested targets and invoke a simulated lethal tool. We find two concerning failure modes. First, some LLM agents invoke the lethal tool for ordinary generic descriptors such as \emph{people}, requiring no jailbreak at all. Second, an agent that initially appears conservative under protected descriptors can become unsafe under a simple semantic target shift.

title: From Data Room to Report: End-to-End AI Support for M&A Legal Due Diligence
authors: Johannes R. Hübers, Daniel Uedelhoven, Manuela Bergau, Markus Beyer, Lars Weber, Tobias Riethmüller, Arkadiusz Rzepka, Tobias Schuh, Maximilian Glaß, Omer Faruk Aydin, Jens Henneberg, Thiago Bell Felix de Oliveira, Lars Hillebrand, Rafet Sifa
abstract: Legal due diligence in mergers and acquisitions requires lawyers to organize heterogeneous virtual data room documents, extract transaction-relevant information and consolidate reviewed findings into a due diligence report. We present LEXI (Legal Extraction and Intelligence), a work-in-progress system that demonstrates how large language models can support this process from document ingestion to report preparation. LEXI classifies documents under a configurable due diligence taxonomy, assigns relevant target entities, extracts predefined information with supporting passages and page-level provenance and prepares report content from reviewed findings. Structured outputs connect these stages and allow model-generated results to be passed through the workflow in a controlled form. Lawyers review and correct classifications and extractions and retain responsibility for legal assessments, recommendations, risk ratings and final report wording. Initial evaluations of the classification and extraction components provide preliminary evidence that the approach is feasible. LEXI illustrates how AI can be integrated across the legal due diligence workflow while preserving lawyer control over substantive legal judgment.

title: CoTacWAM: Joint Modeling of Vision and Touch for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Lei Jin, Yiding Ma, Zhuohang Li, Jiachen Liu, Zibo Zhu, Kairui Liu, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Yong Li
abstract: We present CoTacWAM, a world-action model that learns shared contact semantics between wrist vision and touch, achieving the best observed performance in our nominal manipulation and missing-input evaluations. The two modalities observe the same local interaction through different signals: wrist images reveal nearby geometry, while touch records physical contact. Our approach connects their common contact meaning while preserving the evidence unique to each modality, giving the policy a joint description of interaction across available input combinations. This representation supports predictive action learning alongside head-view scene context and conditions corrections after an independent detector confirms a failed attempt. Experiments across four real-world tasks demonstrate improved manipulation performance over the evaluated baselines, robustness to missing local observations, and further gains from autonomous retries.

title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
authors: Alexander Hock, Sergey Shadrin
abstract: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.

title: A family of forcings with hyperfinite equivalence of generics
authors: Ben De Bondt
abstract: We identify a class of forcings that includes several classical forcings and prove that for all forcings $\mathbb{P}$ in this class the associated equivalence of generics relation $\equiv^{\mathbb{P}}_M$, as defined by Smythe, is a hyperfinite CBER.

title: Proceedings of "Accelerating ALICE background simulations: A WGAN Approach to slow-neutron induced TPC loopers" CHEP 2026, 26/05/2026
authors: Marco Giacalone, Sandro Christian Wenzel, Mesut Arslandok, Andreas Morsch for the ALICE Collaboration
abstract: The simulation of background processes in high-energy physics can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. To provide the most realistic data description at the ALICE experiment using Monte Carlo simulations, we investigated alternative solutions to generate the products of electromagnetic interactions initiated by slow neutrons in the Time Projection Chamber (TPC). Specifically, electrons and positrons from these processes can spiral repeatedly within the magnetic field in the detector (so-called "loopers") and tracking them via full transport frameworks, such as GEANT4, requires extensive computing resources. A fast simulation framework based on a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN) was developed to speed up the simulation process. Our solution is designed to bypass the significant computational cost associated with transporting neutrons to low energies by directly generating the kinematic properties (e.g., momentum, production vertex) of the resulting electron-positron pairs (from neutron capture) and electrons from Compton scattering. The generative model successfully reproduces the complex multidimensional distributions of the background tracks with high fidelity, maintaining agreement with the full GEANT4 simulation. By replacing the full transport of these specific background components with the WGAN inference, a tenfold speedup is achieved, making the simulation of loopers a negligible component of the total processing time. Moreover, the fast simulation framework is modular, allowing for the future inclusion of other background sources, such as nuclear spallation products.

title: Will AI Replace Juniors? How Task Complexity Reduces Automation Risk
authors: Vincent Rost, Fabian Stephany
abstract: How does task complexity shape firms' willingness to substitute entry-level labour with artificial intelligence (AI) tools? We study this question using a pre-registered survey experiment with managers from 1,435 German firms in the information economy and manufacturing industry. Managers are randomly assigned to consider a long lasting need for additional capacity involving either well-structured and standardised tasks, or more complex tasks that require professional judgement, contextual knowledge and independent problem-solving. Relative to standardised tasks, complex tasks reduce willingness to use AI rather than hire an entry-level employee by 0.54 points on a five-point scale and increase the importance attached to human oversight by 0.15 points. Further, pre-treatment responses indicate that managers expect the availability of AI applications to reduce hiring of both entry-level employees and experienced workers, but significantly more strongly for entry-level workers.

title: Higher derivatives and ghosts through three centuries
authors: Andrei Smilga
abstract: We outline the history of the research of dynamic systems including higher derivatives in the Lagrangian, The story starts in 1744 when Euler published a book where the Euler--Lagrange differential equations for a HD system were first written. The next important landmarks were the papers of Ostrogradsky (1850) and of Pais and Uhlenbeck (1950). Many articles written in the second half of the last century were influenced by a misconception that was widespread at the time --- it was believed that higher derivatives necessarily bring about a violation of unitarity. We understand today that this is not the case and there are many systems with benign ghosts where HD are present but unitarity is not violated. In this review, we present and discuss several examples of such (quantum) mechanical systems and 2D field theories. Then we will briefly discuss higher-derivative gravity theories in 4 dimensions. In that case, the question whether the ghosts there are benign or not has a special status due to the absence of a nonperturbative Hamiltonian and does not have a definite answer yet. However, if one restricts oneself to classical theory, one can argue that the ghosts {\it are} benign (benign classical ghostly system is a system that needs an infinite time to reach a singularity, and it seems to the case both in ordinary and in HD gravity: the cosmic censorship conjecture implies that the singularities are always surrounded by horizons, and it takes an infinite time on the clocks of a distant observer to reach a horizon). Finally, I discuss supersymmetric HD theories: conformal supergravity, where the ghosts are also probably benign, and then an interesting supersymmetric HD gauge theory in 6 dimensions. It involves a dimensionless coupling constant, is renormalizable and rather beautiful. Unfortunately, it is not unitary --- ghosts are not benign there.

title: Silent on Code? A Computing Lens on Generative AI Guidance at Canadian Polytechnics and Research Universities
authors: Marco Ho, Michael Pin-Chuan Lin, Rishva Riteshkumar Amin, Daniel Chang, Jeeho Ryoo
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools now write, explain, and debug code, which changes how computing students learn and how their work is assessed. Instructors, however, act within institutional guidance written largely with essays in mind. We report a document analysis of the public, institution-level GenAI guidance of the 13 members of Polytechnics Canada and the 15 members of the U15 Group of Canadian Research Universities, retrieved in October 2026. Using a 27-item codebook spanning governance, integrity and assessment, data and legal issues, values, AI literacy, and a computing lens, we find that both sectors leave course-level decisions to instructors, although polytechnics more often prohibit use unless the instructor permits it (8 of 13 vs. 4 of 14), and converge on disclosure, links to academic integrity policy, and, in most institutions, the expectation that programs adapt rules to their discipline. Polytechnics frame GenAI as workforce preparation substantively far more often (7 of 13 vs. 0 of 14), whereas universities more often address assessment redesign. Twelve of 27 institutions with retrievable guidance mention code, but almost always as one output type among many; none names an AI coding assistant or provides substantive code-specific guidance on attribution, assessment, or licensing. Institution-level guidance is thus not silent on code but leaves programming-specific questions largely to programs and instructors. We propose five elements of discipline-level guidance for computing and release our codebook and coded dataset.

title: Exploring the Design Factors of Pixel-space Diffusion
authors: Mang Ning, Le Zhang, Albert Ali Salah, Itir Onal Ertugrul, Jintao Zhang
abstract: In this paper, we introduce EiT by exploring the key design factors of pixel-space diffusion from three perspectives: model architecture, representation, and frequency domain. Inspired by Denoising Autoencoders (DAE) which perform denoising through a bottleneck, we construct a U-shaped pixel diffusion transformer that performs explicit compression along the channel dimension. In terms of representation, we find that both pixel and latent diffusion transformers exhibit a three-stage representation dynamics across layers and timesteps: denoising/local feature expansion, basis lift-up, and posterior projection. Moreover, earlier denoising and a longer basis lift-up stage are associated with better generation, which EiT naturally achieves through its channel bottleneck and increased network depth. From the frequency perspective, we establish the equivalence between pixel-space and frequency-space diffusion when keeping the network operating in pixel space. On ImageNet $256\times256$ and $512\times512$, EiT consistently outperforms JiT (Just image Transformers) in generation quality. Specifically, our EiT achieves better FID than JiT: 1.61 vs. 1.85 at $256\times256$, and 1.73 vs. 1.99 at $512\times512$. Remarkably, EiT can be seamlessly applied to video pixel diffusion by simply extending the patch size to temporal dimension and outperforms video latent diffusion in FVD evaluated on Kinetics-600 (resolution 256), under comparable total network parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/forever208/EiT

title: Bayesian Calibration of Effective Material Parameters in Electric Machine Stators
authors: Patrick D. Gsoels, Christian M. Riener, Markus Flicker, Jose Romero Lopera, Jan P. Henninger, Bibhu Prasad Nayak, Jan Biermann, Bernhard Auinger, Jan C. Hansen
abstract: Efficiency-driven faster switching by wide-bandgap semiconductor devices increases electromagnetic interference (EMI) in electric vehicles (EVs). Mitigating this EMI becomes more complex as system components grow. Therefore, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is assessed early via system-level simulation of the EV powertrain. A key EMC-critical quantity is the impedance of the electric drive machine, forming a major part of the EMI propagation path. Finite element (FE) simulations are typically used but are computationally expensive and limited by insufficient material property knowledge. We present a surrogate model based Bayesian calibration framework for 3D full-wave FE simulation of an externally excited synchronous motor (EESM) stator. Effective material parameters (EMPs) are calibrated to match broadband differential mode (DM) impedance measurements up to 30 MHz. A multi-output surrogate model replaces the demanding FE simulation, while an orthogonal surrogate model compliant discrepancy term assesses material modeling completeness. Using Hamiltonian Markov Chain Monte Carlo, we construct posterior distributions of the EMPs for three calibration scenarios with different parameter ranges. Two of three scenarios achieve good agreement with measurements. However, accurate calibration requires "datasheet-deviating" EMPs, while "datasheet-aligned" ones yield deficient results, indicating material models do not fully capture the underlying physics. The proposed methodology enables estimating unknown material properties from impedance measurements and evaluates the sufficiency of chosen material models. Although identified EMPs may differ from datasheet values, they reliably estimate frequency-dependent DM impedance. This work focuses on EMPs influencing the stator's DM impedance; complete machine calibration, including rotor and common-mode impedance, is the scope of future research.

title: Toward a quantum resistance standard above liquid nitrogen temperature
authors: Kaining Yang, Changwei Zhai, Naijie Ren, Kai Zhao, Chengyuan Li, Changhao Zhao, Yunfeng Lu, Yaning Wang, Jianting Zhao, Zheng Vitto Han
abstract: Quantum Hall effect (QHE) -- the pioneering demonstration of one-dimensional topologically-protected edge channels -- manifest a transversal resistance quantized solely by two universal constants $e$ and $h$ (the elementary charge and the Planck constant, respectively), referred to as the von Klitzing constant $R_\mathrm{K}=h/e^{2}$. For decades, this has enabled a unique route for realizing quantum Hall resistance (QHR) standard in the Système international d'unitès (SI), yet high precision QHR under relaxed conditions, especially temperature higher than 30 K, has not been possible. Here, we show that interfacial charge-order coupling inbetween CrOCl and monolayer graphene offers enhanced Fermi velocity, creating a robust Landau cyclotron gap. Using a customized direct current comparator (DCC, mounted at room temperature), we obtain relative deviation of the Hall resistance from $R_\mathrm{K}/2$ of (15 $\pm$ 23)\,n$Ω$ $Ω$$^{-1}$ (23 parts per billion of relative uncertainty) at 50 K, with an external magnetic field of 12 T and a dc current of 10 $μ$A. At 100 K, the system exhibits QHR with 2 parts per million of relative uncertainty. Our results therefore suggest a platform toward a next-generation quantum resistance standard that may work at above liquid nitrogen temperature and free of conventional compressor refrigerators.

title: When to Respond, Where to Ground: Streaming 3D Affordance Grounding
authors: Wenting Luan, Weilong Yan, Siqi Lu, Ming Li, Beibei Lin, Yongbin Zheng, Robby T. Tan
abstract: Given a continuous RGB-D stream and a language request, streaming 3D affordance grounding requires an agent to decide when to respond and where to locate the requested functional part using only observations available so far. Existing 3D affordance grounding methods typically assume complete scene observations, while streaming vision-language models lack fine-grained 3D functional grounding. Our goal is to jointly determine response timing and functional-part localization during continuous scene observation. We propose StreamAff, an evidence-guided response strategy that makes both decisions from the grounding model's own visual evidence. The model scores the visual patches of the frames it reads: their combined support, weighed against a wait option, decides when to respond, and the highest-scoring patch selects the frame to ground in. A conditional look-back policy lets the model answer from an earlier observation at the moment of the request or wait for new evidence, and zoom-and-refine grounding segments the part named in the answer on the 3D points of the selected frame. We further introduce StreamFun3D, a benchmark derived from real-world 3D scenes that evaluates response timing and grounding across four evidence settings: Current, History, Future, and Unobserved, together with StreamIoU, a metric that credits a mask only when the response is timely and grounded in a valid source frame. We adapt offline 3D affordance grounding methods and build external-decider baselines that pair vision-language models with our mask decoder. StreamAff achieves 30.14% StreamIoU on 15-second streams, a 40.6% relative improvement over the strongest of these baselines.

title: Gradient Optical Diffraction Tomography Using Deep Learning-Assisted Amplitude Estimation
authors: Julianna Winnik, Piotr Zdańkowski, Konrad Kosuge, Aleksandra Parys, Marzena Stefaniuk, Junwei Min, Baoli Yao, Maciej Trusiak
abstract: Gradient Optical Diffraction Tomography (GODT) enables the non-invasive reconstruction of a spatial derivative of the 3D sample's refractive index distribution, providing enhanced sensitivity to subtle refractive index variations through gradient-based contrast. Implemented using lateral shearing interferometry (LSI), GODT benefits from a common-path architecture that provides environmental stability and high signal-to-noise ratio measurements. Unlike conventional optical diffraction tomography (ODT), which requires numerical integration of LSI-derived phase gradients to recover the object phase, GODT enables direct tomographic reconstruction from the LSI data. Notably, GODT requires derivatives of both the phase and amplitude of the object fields as input. While the phase derivative can be readily extracted from LSI data, the amplitude gradient cannot be directly retrieved. Thus, in the original GODT formulation, the amplitude gradient was assumed to be negligible, limiting the accuracy of the resulting 3D reconstruction. In this work, we introduce amplitude-informed GODT (AI-GODT), which employs physics-informed supervised deep learning to estimate the missing amplitude gradient based on accessible LSI data, specifically the fringe modulation. The proposed approach, applying a ResNet architecture and training on computer-generated data, is validated through numerical simulation and experimental measurements of both a well-characterized test object and primary neuronal cell culture, demonstrating the network's ability to generalize to diverse samples. We show that incorporation of the recovered amplitude gradient into the GODT reconstruction pipeline improves the 3D reconstruction quality, especially in its out-of-focus regions. The software and datasets are openly available to facilitate reproducibility and further development.

title: Nonparametric predictive inference for interval-censored data: M-functions anchored to the self-consistent estimator
authors: M. T. Loots, F. P. A. Coolen
abstract: Nonparametric predictive inference specifies the distribution of a future observation through M-functions, which are basic probability assignments on intervals. Here such a specification is proposed for data censored on the left, on the right or within intervals of arbitrary width. It is the union of two M-functions. The first rests on a post-data assumption under which each censored observation divides its predictive mass equally amongst the observations with regions inside its own, and it reproduces the right-censored theory exactly. The second combines the Turnbull estimator with one unconstrained unit of predictive mass. The resulting survival bounds contain the Turnbull estimator, lie inside the bounds from all completions of the data and need no enumeration. In simulated inspection schemes they were calibrated for fixed events and for the rank of a further observation, while the second member alone was not. Equal weights on all orderings allowed by the data give the first member whenever the regions are nested or disjoint. The method is compared with the Turnbull estimator on two interval-censored studies.

title: On pseudo-null Iwasawa modules, restricted ramification, and Non-freeness Conjecture over a quartic CM-field
authors: Takuya Yanagisawa
abstract: Let $k$ be a CM-field of degree greater than $2$, $p$ an odd prime number that splits completely in $k$, and $Σ$ a $p$-adic CM-type of $k$. In this setting, we show the non-triviality of the $Σ$-ramified Iwasawa module of the maximal multiple $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension $\widetilde{k}/k$. As a consequence, under a weak form of Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture, we see that the unramified Iwasawa module and the $Σ$-ramified Iwasawa module of $\widetilde{k}$ never coincide. In the case where $k$ is a quartic CM-field, under a certain assumption, we show that the non-coincidence condition is equivalent to Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture. We also study a relation of the non-coincidence condition with Non-freeness Conjecture, which is a conjecture studied in non-abelian Iwasawa theory.

title: Three-dimensional harmonic critical metrics for the Einstein-Hilbert functional and self-similar Ricci flows
authors: Sergey E. Stepanov, Irina I. Tsyganok
abstract: We address the three-dimensional harmonic analogue of Hilbert's variational problem: does criticality of the Einstein-Hilbert functional under volume-preserving Chen-Nagano variations force constant sectional curvature, and how is this rigidity related to Ricci flow and topology? Starting from the known characterization of compact harmonic critical metrics as gradient Ricci solitons, we use Ivey's classification to show that such metrics on closed three manifolds are precisely the space-form metrics, equivalently the stationary metrics of the volume-normalized Ricci flow. We also describe residual gauge one-forms, establish transversality of the Chen-Nagano gauge to infinitesimal diffeomorphism directions, and give explicit self-similar flows. The normalized Ricci-flow velocity is an admissible Chen-Nagano variation for n > = 3, and the smooth Poincar'e theorem admits an equivalent formulation in terms of the existence of harmonic critical metrics

title: Kiselev black hole from semiclassical gravity with conformal anomaly
authors: Yu-Sen An, Yu-Lin Chen
abstract: Investigating black hole physics in semi-classical gravitational theory is an interesting and important direction. When the backreaction of the conformal anomaly-induced effective stress-energy tensor is taken into account, the black hole spacetime can be largely altered which changes many properties of the black hole. In this work, rather than restricting our attention to the type-A anomaly, we incorporate the type-B anomaly and investigate how it modifies the spacetime structure obtained when only the type-A anomaly is considered. We find that for a specific relation between the central charges and the cosmological constant, the semiclassical Einstein equations can be solved analytically, yielding a metric that takes the exact form of the Kiselev black hole. After deriving the solution, we further discuss the properties of this new black hole solutions. Our work serves as an essential stepping stone for studying black hole geometries under the full conformal anomaly.

title: Evaluating Ukrainian Grammatical Competence in Language Models: Probability Versus Prompting
authors: Dmytro Babarytskyi, Oleksandr Babarytskyi, Vadym Savanevych
abstract: Organisations deploying large language models in Ukrainian-language information systems need to know whether a model produces normative Ukrainian. This paper establishes a protocol for measuring that reliably and applies it to 19 models. The instrument is a released set of 1,444 Ukrainian minimal pairs covering the vocative case, numeral-noun and adjective agreement, verb government and calques from russian, with subject-verb agreement as a control; a quarter of the set was checked against the answer key in two independent native-speaker ratings, which agreed at Cohen's $κ$ = 0.963. Every pair is scored twice: by comparing the probabilities a model assigns to the two sentences, and by asking the model directly, with the sentences presented in both orders so that answer-position effects are measured instead of being absorbed into the score. Three results follow. Order consistency (the share of pairs answered identically when the sentences are exchanged) falls below 0.05 for ten of the nineteen models, and what separates the usable models is instruction tuning, not scale. The vocative case is systematically inverted: 0.153 accuracy against 0.951 on the control, with models preferring the non-normative nominative form of address. Ukrainian adaptation substantially reduces this deficit, measured against the exact checkpoints two adapted models were trained from.

title: Manga Page Parser: Comprehensive Visual Parsing through Local Story Understanding
authors: Yingxuan Li, Jiafeng Mao, Arata Furukawa, Mayu Otani
abstract: Understanding manga requires connecting who appears and who speaks with the events, character states, and relationships that unfold across panels. We study manga visual parsing through local story understanding: analyzing each double-page spread independently to capture and organize its story information in a reusable structured representation. We propose MangaParser, an agentic reading framework that jointly performs character clustering, speaker diarization, and speaker-to-character binding within a shared multimodal conversation, without additional training or fine-tuning. The agent uses structured story memory to guide character and speaker identification, inspecting relevant image regions when uncertain and refining its predictions and story records together as evidence accumulates. Quantitative evaluations show that our parser substantially outperforms manga-specific models across multiple backbones. Parsing examples illustrate how a unified representation links the character and speaker predictions with narrative content and supporting evidence. We further test reusability through story question answering using outputs generated before the questions are provided. The results confirm output reusability, offering a foundation for manga translation, content retrieval, and question answering.

title: Rotation curves of dwarf galaxies and dark matter as a condensate of $q$-deformed bosons: reconstruction and fits of the deformation profile
authors: Mahnaz Maleki, Asef Kheirandish, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, Hosein Mohammadzadeh
abstract: Dark-matter-dominated dwarf galaxies are a sensitive testing ground for models in which dark matter is a self-interacting Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). In the Thomas-Fermi limit the standard BEC halo has the density profile $ρ\propto\sin(kr)/(kr)$, so that the shape of its rotation curve is fixed up to two scale parameters. Here we consider a condensate of $q$-deformed bosons. We show that, in the Thomas-Fermi limit, the deformation enters the structure of the halo only through the chemical potential of the condensate; consequently, a spatially uniform deformation parameter leaves the standard BEC profile unchanged. In every galaxy $χ$ is depressed in the inner region, $kr\lesssim1$, relative to the outer halo, where it is approximately constant in most cases: the standard condensate describes the outer halo, while the core requires a weaker deformation, i.e., $q$ closer to unity. The profiles share this qualitative shape, but neither the depth nor the width of the depression is universal. Modelling the depression by a Gaussian, with two additional parameters, we fit the rotation curves with rms residuals of $0.6$--$2.6$~km\,s$^{-1}$, against $1.6$--$8.5$~km\,s$^{-1}$ for the standard condensate. According to the Bayesian information criterion, the deformed condensate is preferred over the standard condensate, the Navarro-Frenk-White profile, and the Burkert profile in four galaxies, is indistinguishable from the best of them in two, and is disfavoured in two. We discuss the limitations of these results, in particular the absence of error bars in the data, the neglect of baryons, and the phenomenological status of a position-dependent deformation.

title: An Electromagnetic Ergoregion Limits the Reconnection-Driven Penrose Process
authors: Qian Wan, Yehui Hou, Yu Song, Jing-Ze Xia, Yosuke Mizuno, Bin Chen
abstract: Magnetic reconnection taps black-hole rotational energy via negative-energy ejecta, but field geometry itself can forbid such ejection inside the spacetime ergoregion. We identify a covariant electromagnetic (EM) ergoregion for general degenerate, magnetically dominated fields in stationary spacetimes. Outside the EM ergoregion, even ultrarelativistic field-guided ejecta cannot attain negative Killing energy. For Alfvénic reconnection outflows, the magnetization threshold scales inversely with the transverse distance to the EM ergosurface. The mass-loaded Kerr model places the EM ergosurface at about 75% of the radial interval from the horizon to the spacetime ergosurface, close to the time-averaged boundary inferred from a dynamical simulation. Together, these results show that field geometry determines where negative-energy ejection is possible, while magnetization sets the threshold for realizing it.

title: FasterGRN: Reducing the Refinement Redundancy for Accelerating Generative Refinement Networks
authors: Ziqian Zhang, Pengcheng Wang, Yulong Chen, Yaxing Wang, Senmao Li, Kai Wang
abstract: Departing from the paradigm of diffusion and autoregressive models, Generative Refinement Networks (GRN) enables high-quality image generation through iterative refinements. However, this repeated processing over the entire visual representations results in substantial computation overhead. Furthermore, the binary representations and global refinement mechanism in GRN disable the direct application of acceleration strategies developed for other generative models. To accelerate GRN model, we first observe several key properties by analyzing the entire generative process. That includes the stage characteristic, dual branch similarity and more importantly, the $\textbf{refinement redundancy}$. Motivated by the observations, we present $\textbf{FasterGRN}$, a training-free acceleration method for the Generative Refinement Network. $\textbf{FasterGRN}$ first divides the GRN into the semantic establishment stage and detail refinement stage according to its semantic establishment. For alleviating the refinement redundancy mainly resulting from the detail refinement stage, we propose Adaptive Retention Expansion ($\textbf{ARE}$) and Selective Token Freezing ($\textbf{STF}$) to shrink refinement steps and reduce token computations, respectively. In the experiments on GenEval and DPG-Bench benchmarks, our method $\textbf{FasterGRN}$ achieves a $2.03\times$ sampling speedup while largely preserving image generation performance. Our evaluation on COCO datasets additionally demonstrates that $\textbf{FasterGRN}$ even outperforms the original GRN in image fidelity.

title: DLaR: Dynamic Stochasticity Control for Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
authors: Xiaocheng Luo, Peng Xu, Zaifu Zhan, Xiangyu Duan
abstract: Latent reasoning enables LLMs to operate in continuous embedding space, yet existing methods suffer from deterministic inference that precludes exploration of diverse reasoning paths. While recent approaches inject stochasticity to restore exploration, we identify two fundamental limitations: \textit{uniform stochasticity} across all steps is suboptimal, and unconstrained perturbations disrupt reasoning coherence. We propose Dynamic Stochasticity Control for Latent Reasoning (DLaR), a framework with two complementary mechanisms that operate at different temporal granularities within the GRPO reinforcement learning framework. At the token level, Adaptive Stochasticity Modulation (ASM) dynamically adjusts perturbation intensity at each latent step based on a confidence-entropy fusion signal, increasing exploration when the model is uncertain and preserving stability when confident. At the training level, Training-Aware Stochasticity Tuning (TAST) progressively decays the base stochasticity level following a curriculum schedule. Through this dual-level design, DLaR establishes a hierarchical exploration-exploitation strategy that operates at both token and training levels. Extensive experiments on four in-distribution and three out-of-distribution mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that DLaR achieves the highest average performance across model scales, reaching 27.9%/50.6% Pass@1/Pass@8 on Llama-3.2-1B and 46.8%/68.2% on Qwen2.5-1.5B. Code: \href{https://github.com/xiaocen-luo/DLaR}{https://github.com/xiaocen-luo/DLaR}.

title: On Shepp's property in free probability
authors: Wiktor Ejsmont, Takahiro Hasebe, Patrycja Hęćka-Jędraszczyk
abstract: We establish a free analogue of Shepp's theorem for freely independent standard semicircular elements. We show more generally that a family of self-normalized squared quadratic forms is free, and each has a standard Marchenko-Pastur distribution. The free analogue of Shepp's theorem follows by taking the coefficients of quadratic forms to be the three Pauli matrices. We also prove some new free analogues of Lukacs-type independence results. The key part of the proof is a construction of an equivalent and simpler operator model on a corner algebra compressed by a free projection.

title: Where Does Free-Text 3D Grounding Fail? An Error Analysis of Report-Sentence Segmentation in Chest CT
authors: Abdullah Arif Sheikh, Kamalaker Dadi, Raju S. Bapi
abstract: Free-text 3D grounding, segmenting in a CT volume the region described by one sentence of the radiology report, could link reports to images at scale, but it is unclear where current models fail. We analyse the publicly released VoxTell model on all 381 findings of the 200-scan ReXGroundingCT validation set, where it grounds 53.5% of findings. Its failures are rarely about which lesion or side is meant. No miss lies on the side opposite to the one named, and findings are almost never confused with one another. Instead, predictions are too large, land on a neighbouring lesion on the correct side, or are missing for small findings, and diffuse findings are rarely grounded. Removing location words halves performance, to the level of label-only prompting, and anatomical rules derived from the sentence never improve the full-sentence output. The same pattern holds on the hidden 300-scan test set. Further progress therefore depends on extent estimation and small-lesion sensitivity rather than on anatomical post-processing.

title: A Graphical Criterion for Linear Causal Bounds
authors: Alexis Bellot
abstract: The values of causal effects and counterfactuals are typically only partially identified from observational data in the presence of unobserved confounding. With discretely-valued variables, under certain conditions, sharp bounds can be derived by solving one linear program. This is then computationally tractable for many causal questions. In this paper, for every diagram in which each confounded component has at most two hidden causes, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the sharp bounds to be equal to the optimum of one linear program for every (positive) input probability table. This algorithm is implemented in a new Python package, called "partialid", that allows users to compose assumptions, queries, and data to obtain sharp bounds in a computationally tractable manner.

title: The Illusion of an Automated German Census: Assessing the Feasibility of the 2031 Register-Based Census via Simulation
authors: R. Schnell, S. V. Weiand
abstract: The next German Census (2031) is planned to be the country's first fully register-based census, relying exclusively on administrative data sources. In addition to the population registers, ten further administrative registers are envisaged, covering a wide range of information, from driving licences to agricultural social insurance. This study simulates potential data-quality challenges in linking these registers using quasi-identifiers (QIDs), such as names and dates of birth. Using a synthetic population dataset (N=80,206,770), we systematically vary experimental factors related to register characteristics. Across the 1,458 experimental conditions studied, results vary considerably. Some plausible scenarios range from 500,000 to 1,000,000 false-negative linkage errors per linked register. These findings suggest that implementing an automated register-based census using the currently envisaged registers may prove challenging and could require substantial manual post-processing to achieve acceptable data quality.

title: Mass Spectral Evidence for Iron Sulfate in Venus' Cloud Aerosol
authors: Rakesh Mogul, Mikhail Yu. Zolotov, Michael J. Way, Sanjay S. Limaye
abstract: Venus' cloud aerosols play pivotal roles in the thermal, chemical, and optical properties of the atmosphere. Here, we present mass spectral evidence that the cloud aerosols contain abundant iron sulfates. Data from the Pioneer Venus Large Probe Neutral Mass Spectrometer (LNMS) suggest that cloud aerosols inadvertently collected into the inlets at ~48-51 km and thermally decomposed below the clouds, releasing several compounds into the LNMS. At 23 km and below, multiple iron species (54Fe+, 56FeO+, 54FeO+, 56Fe2O+, and 56Fe2O2+) and other decomposition gases were detected. Quantitative treatment of these mass signals suggested the release of Fe2O3, SO2, O2, SO3, H2SO4, and H2O, consistent with the thermal decomposition of hydronium-bearing ferric sulfates. The resulting mole ratio for iron to sulfate (2.0 +/- 1.1) aligns with hydronium jarosite ((H3O)Fe3(SO4)2(OH)6), which likely formed within the inlets after aerosol capture, dehydration, and loss of sulfuric acid. Our thermochemical calculations support these assessments. Speciation of the ferric sulfates in the native aerosols remains unconstrained (e.g., solution and/or particle phases). Peak fits to the thermal release profiles yielded the abundances of the bulk iron (0.8 +/- 0.4 mg m-3) and aerosol-derived compounds, including hydronium jarosite (2.2 +/- 1.2 mg m-3, 30 +/- 17 wt%), water (3.7 +/- 0.4 mg m-3, 50 +/- 10 wt%), and sulfuric acid (1.5 +/- 0.2 mg m-3, 20 +/- 5 wt%). Surface sourcing of the cloud iron is likely minor. Instead, cosmic dust influx could deliver iron to the clouds in a geologically short time (2.4 +/- 1.5 Myr).

title: Multiwavelength Analysis of the Merging Cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8: A Three-way Merger in Disguise?
authors: Rodrigo Stancioli, David Wittman, Kyle Finner, Faik Bouhrik, Zhuoran Gao
abstract: We identify the galaxy cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8 as a candidate bimodal merging cluster due to its optical properties listed in the redMaPPer cluster catalog. To confirm the cluster's merging state and reveal its dark matter halo and intracluster medium (ICM) morphologies, we conducted a multiwavelength follow-up campaign encompassing HST/ACS optical observations, XMM-Newton X-ray imaging, and Keck/Deimos multislit spectroscopy. The weak lensing mass reconstruction performed with the HST images shows two resolved peaks whose positions coincide with the two brightest cluster galaxies. The ICM morphology is consistent with a post-pericenter merger, with significant asymmetry in X-ray flux between subclusters. Our Keck/Deimos redshift measurements reveal a relative velocity $Δv_{\mathrm{LOS}} = 480$ km s$^{-1}$ between eastern and western subclusters. The eastern, more massive subcluster, however, exhibits a highly elongated shape, suggesting either a dark matter halo of considerable eccentricity or the presence of a third, unresolved halo, eliciting the question of whether RMJ1219 is truly binary or a three-way merger. To investigate these hypotheses, we fit the weak lensing shear data using four different combinations of spherical and elliptical NFW halo models and provide an estimate of the mass and concentration of each subhalo. Although the best fit is achieved with a three-halo model, the data are insufficient to determine whether the introduction of extra parameters is statistically justified.

title: Almost sure lower bound for the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of critical AMO
authors: Yanhui Qu, Pengyu Wang
abstract: We show that there exists an absolute constant $d>0$ such that for almost all frequencies $α\in[0,1]\setminus\Q$, the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of the critical almost Mathieu operator $H_{1,α,θ}$ is bounded from below by $d$.

title: Monte Carlo-based secondary dose check platform for the world's first ultra-compact upright proton therapy system
authors: Toghrul Alakbarzade, Emir Musa Olgun, Yuan James Rao, Billy W Loo, Adam Johansson, Yong Yang, Murat Surucu, Mehmet Burcin Unlu, Serdar Charyyev
abstract: Objective. This work aimed to develop and validate an independent Monte Carlo (MC) secondary dose check of the RayStation treatment planning system (TPS) for the Mevion S250-FIT, the world's first ultra-compact upright proton therapy system. Approach. The treatment nozzle, including the energy modulation system of boron carbide and polycarbonate plates and the adaptive aperture, was modeled in the TOPAS (TOol for PArticle Simulation) MC code, and the beam model was commissioned against integrated depth dose curves, in-air spot profiles, and dose per monitor unit measured at 12 energy settings. Based on this model, an in-house converter, RayStation2TOPAS, recalculates the TPS plans by reconstructing each pencil beam spot, the aperture for each energy layer, and the seated patient's rotation. In total, 15 water phantom plans and 25 clinical plans were recalculated and compared with the TPS by the point dose, with a tolerance of 5%, and by three-dimensional gamma analysis at 3%/2mm, with a pass rate of at least 90%. Main results. The simulated proton range agreed with the measurement within 0.25mm, the spot full width at half maximum within 6.8%, and the dose per monitor unit within 1.3%. The point dose differed from the TPS by -0.76% to +1.98% in the water phantom plans and by -3.03% to +3.99% in the clinical plans, with gamma pass rates of 96.39% to 99.93% and 90.08% to 99.98%, so every plan passed both tests. Significance. To our knowledge, this is the first independent MC secondary dose check for the S250-FIT, and it complements measurement-based patient-specific quality assurance of its plans.

title: UPP-Gauss: Ultrasound Propagation Physics-informed Gaussian Splatting for B-mode Novel-View Synthesis
authors: Guil Jung, Seok-Hwan Oh, Myeong-Gee Kim, Young-Min Kim, Hyeon-Jik Lee, Sang-Yun Kim, Hyeok-Jun Kwon, Hyuk-Sool Kwon, Hyeon-Min Bae
abstract: Accurate novel-view synthesis of B-mode ultrasound images requires modeling acoustic propagation through tissue and the resulting appearance variations across probe poses. We propose Ultrasound Propagation Physics-informed Gaussian Splatting (UPP-Gauss), which integrates these acoustic interactions into an explicit Gaussian representation. UPP-Gauss constructs acoustic maps by sampling three 3D Gaussian fields using the probe pose and acoustic beam propagation direction, then combines these maps according to ultrasound propagation to synthesize B-mode images. Across three acoustically diverse datasets, UPP-Gauss achieves the best reconstruction quality with efficient rendering, improving PSNR over the best baseline on each dataset by 1.43 dB on average. These results demonstrate accurate and efficient B-mode novel-view synthesis through explicit Gaussian modeling of ultrasound propagation.

title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
authors: Zeyang Guan, Qihao Zhao, Rui Gong, Zhang Haitian, Yalun Dai, Yangyu Huang, Lingao Xiao, Haozhe Du, Xuehui Yu, Ye Lu, Jianjun Gao, Ruoyu Wang, Haowen Bai, Hao Li, Scarlett Li, Kim-Hui Yap
abstract: General-purpose multimodal foundation models enable robots to adapt during deployment from observations and execution feedback, without task-specific demonstrations or training. However, the robot retains what it learns only in the model's working context. Once the task ends, it loses this execution knowledge, such as how to carry a bowl between two grippers. On the next attempt at the task, the robot may take just as long and repeat the same mistakes. To avoid this repetition, robots must retain execution knowledge across attempts. Yet replaying past actions is insufficient, because their effects depend on the current conditions. Procedures that determine actions from the current scene address this, but when they meet conditions that earlier attempts did not cover, revising them requires the measured effects of earlier actions. We therefore propose SEEK, an agentic framework that retains both, enabling robots to improve across attempts while keeping the underlying model fixed. To adapt retained knowledge to the current scene, SEEK adopts a Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy (SEPP) that encodes manipulation as executable procedures and determines each action from current observations. As the robot executes these procedures, SEEK records the measured effects of its actions, including those from failed attempts, in a Persistent Action-Effect Bank (PAEB). Where a retained procedure applies, it acts without a model request; where it meets a condition it does not cover, this evidence guides its revision. On RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks. On 34 of these tasks with GPT-6.2 Astra, SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts, against 49.6 for the same model acting directly, and uses 77.6% fewer model requests. https://zeyangguan.github.io/SEEK-Agentic-Robot-Manipulation/

title: X-World: Transferring Video Priors to Cross-Embodiment Robot Control
authors: Chun Gu, Xiaofei Wei, Yiming Chen, Juntong Zhang, Li Zhang
abstract: Language-instructed manipulation requires robust closedloop policies, yet action-labeled robot trajectories are costly and limited in coverage. Human and robot videos provide complementary spatiotemporal priors for crossembodiment control. We propose X-World, which adapts pretrained video diffusion to variable views. A Q-Former compresses hidden states into tokens for a shared flowmatching expert that predicts action chunks. Datasetspecific projections map native states and actions. We adapt the backbone on large-scale robot and human videos, freeze it for action-only pretraining of the Q-Former and action expert, then post-train on the target platform. At inference, X-World responds at 20 Hz and overlaps updates with execution via asynchronous real-time chunking. X-World performs strongly on LIBERO and under zero-shot shifts on LIBERO-Plus. On hardware, it averages 81.7% success across six bimanual tasks on the side-mounted dual-arm UR5e, one of three real-robot configurations presented.

title: Free boundary MHD equilibria with surface tension
authors: Chengchun Hao
abstract: Free boundary equilibria of an ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) plasma, at rest, with surface tension and an exterior vacuum are studied. Within the frozen-in orbit of a reference magnetic field, every equilibrium is a critical point of the magnetic plus surface energy over the space of volume-preserving embeddings; the capillary boundary condition is the first-variation boundary term, and no assumption on the connectivity of the boundary is required. In the plane the frozen-in law fixes the distribution of the stream function and turns the energy into a rearrangement functional. For a single-axis reference field a sharp lower bound is proved that depends only on that distribution and is attained by an explicit area-preserving diffeomorphism, smooth across the axis, which yields a classical equilibrium. For Morse stream functions sharper bounds governed by the level-set topology are obtained, with a strict gap at an isolated simple saddle merge. In three dimensions no such reduction is available: the energy does not control the full gradient of the embedding, no scalar rearrangement principle applies, and the axisymmetric reduction yields only a conditional lower bound.

title: MoS: Mixture-of-Modality Streaming for Low-Latency Online Video LLM Analytics over Dynamic Networks
authors: Zekai Li, Xiaoyi Fan, Yifei Zhu
abstract: The serving model for next-generation video analytics systems is shifting from traditional task-specific vision models to general-purpose online video Large Language Models (LLMs). Online video LLMs enable flexible, contextual understanding of continuously arriving video content via natural language. However, their substantial resource requirements typically mandate cloud-based inference, making continuous video streaming from user devices necessary to keep the cloud model's context current for online interaction. This introduces significant challenges under existing dynamic and often harsh networks, degrading both accuracy and responsiveness in latency-sensitive applications. In this paper, we propose MoS, a new streaming system that adaptively streams a combination of visual and derived textual modalities over fluctuating networks to enable Pareto-optimal video LLM analytics. The key insight is to leverage the complementarity and interchangeability of different modalities, hidden in video LLM, to improve system performance. Concretely, MoS introduces adaptive anchor frame selection and incremental content tracking to enable low-latency text description generation at the device side. A joint profiler characterizes the accuracy and overhead of paired video and textual configurations, including caption input resolution and output-token budget. A stochastic optimization-based modality controller then selects modality combinations and configurations using this profile and the asynchronous latency of the two modalities to adapt to network conditions. Across 500 StreamingBench video-question pairs, 4G/5G uplink traces, and the VideoLLM-Online and DisPider backends, MoS reduces latency violations by up to 94.3% and improves accuracy by up to 60.4% relative to the evaluated streaming baselines.

title: When Are Parallel Subagents Effective for Coding? An Empirical Study on Repository Construction
authors: Zhiheng Lyu, Chengyu Yin, Lingming Zhang
abstract: LLM-based coding agents are increasingly used for long-horizon tasks such as building an entire program from a specification. Products like Codex and Claude Code let an agent delegate work to parallel subagents, multiplying run cost, yet it remains unclear whether and when delegation produces a better program. We compare a single agent with a main agent delegating to subagents on repository-construction tasks from NL2Repo and ProgramBench (which also provides an executable reference program). We compare scores at equal time and equal cost, run intervention experiments, and analyze fine-grained behavior. On randomly drawn tasks, parallel subagents raise hidden-test pass rates by only about 1 to 5 percentage points at up to 3.8x the cost of a single agent. Their gain is larger on hard tasks, where we find evidence of three mechanisms. Self-checking: with GPT-5.6 Sol, one sentence telling a single agent to probe the reference program first recovers most of this gain at a fraction of the cost; from GPT-5.6 Sol to GPT-6.1 Sol, the gain shrinks as single agents check their own work more. Fresh context: in extended runs, a single agent that periodically starts a new session with an empty conversation makes faster early progress in every comparison than one that resumes its conversation. Modularity: multi-agent runs produce more modular code (more files and shorter functions), closer to the upstream source. We observe similar patterns in a smaller replication with Opus 5.5 on Claude Code. Overall, subagents help when (i) a single agent stops checking too early, (ii) a long session keeps editing with little improvement, or (iii) modular code helps on the task; otherwise, they mainly add cost.

title: Cascading LO-phonon-mediated resonant energy transfer from excitons to Eu3+ for ultrahigh color purity red luminescence in europium-doped GaN
authors: Shizhao Fan, Yue Xu, Yuhao Yin, Shitao Dong, Shaoqiang Chen, Xueyuan Chen, Zhan Su, Datao Tu, Qian Sun, Hui Yang
abstract: High-efficiency, wavelength-stable red micro-LEDs with ultrahigh color purity remain a critical bottleneck for monolithic III-nitride full-color displays. Europium-doped GaN (GaN:Eu) offers a compelling solution, yet the microscopic energy transfer mechanism from the GaN host to Eu3+ ions has remained unresolved for three decades, impeding rational performance optimization. Here we report polaron-mediated resonant energy transfer in high-crystalline-quality GaN:Eu epilayers grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. Eu3+ doping stabilizes a distinct bound exciton (BX3) state at 3.478 eV, which couples strongly with longitudinal optical (LO) phonons via the Frohlich interaction to form cascading polarons with up to seven phonon replicas at a uniform energy spacing of 92.0+/-0.7 meV. The BX3 polaron coupled with 5LO phonons matches precisely the 7F0-->5D3 intra-4f transition energy of Eu3+ at 3.019 eV. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence reveals non-equilibrium phonon emission, evidencing directional resonant energy transfer. After rapid nonradiative relaxation from the 5D3 excited state to the 5D0 metastable state, the hypersensitive 5D0-->7F2 transition yields sharp 622 nm red emission. Time-resolved spectroscopy confirms a single dominant Eu3+ luminescent site with reduced local symmetry, attributed to off-axis EuGa-VN complexes. This work identifies a key energy transfer channel and provides a clear framework for designing high-efficiency GaN:Eu red emitter.

title: Decoherent Histories from Local Spectral Dephasing in Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Jie Gu
abstract: We study local spectral dephasing as a mechanism for decoherent histories in isolated quantum many-body systems. We prove that vanishing projector-weighted spectral concentration is asymptotically equivalent to vanishing time-averaged local memory. With independently sampled waiting times and suitable conditions on the initial state and history weights, this local property suppresses normalized interference across complete fixed-length history families with high probability. For translation-invariant lattices, spectral estimates provide conditions under which dephasing occurs at long times. Exact diagonalization and sparse time evolution of a spin chain illustrate the results.

title: Skysail: Altitude Control of Long-Duration Weather Balloons by Extracting Work from Wind Shear
authors: Michal Adamkiewicz, Andrey Sushko
abstract: Long-duration weather balloons collect repeated atmospheric profiles by venting lifting gas and dropping ballast, but these finite consumables limit the number of profiles each balloon can obtain. We present an altitude-control system that extracts mechanical work from atmospheric wind shear. A small wing suspended 450 m below a zero-pressure balloon experiences relative airflow from the wind velocity difference between the two altitudes. Controlling the wing's pitch produces aerodynamic forces that drive ascent and descent. We develop a model for sizing the system, a lightweight aerodynamic governor for tether deployment, and a control architecture for altitude holding and repeated profiling. Flight experiments conducted over two years accurate control of vertical motion. During a 43-hour interval, the system completed eleven profiles and accumulated 53 km of vertical travel without releasing ballast or venting gas. A separate eight-day flight completed 24 profiles exceeding 1 km in vertical extent, accumulating 159 km of vertical travel. Control authority depends on the available wind shear, with conventional ballast and vent actuation retained for trim and fallback control. These results demonstrate that atmospheric wind shear can sustain repeated balloon profiling while reducing dependence on consumable actuators.

title: FORK: Co-Evolving Safe Disclosure and Decision Skills Against Attackers Who Read Every Refusal
authors: Hieu Man, Chao Shang, Rui Dong, Devang Kulshreshtha, Yanjun Qi, Sandesh Swamy
abstract: When a guardrail rejects an LLM agent's action, its message reaches any attacker observing the trajectory: a fixed refusal leaves benign users unable to recover, whereas an explanation can tell the attacker what to try next. We study this as safe disclosure: explaining rejections so that authorized tasks recover without increasing adaptive attack success. Safe disclosure depends on both the decision and the message: what the guardrail blocks and what it reveals to the agent and the attacker. Because hand-written rules alone cannot anticipate how adaptive attackers probe decisions or use messages, we introduce FORK, which co-evolves a guardrail's natural-language decision and disclosure skills with an attacker that reads every public message. Each exploited message and permissive decision gives FORK evidence for a gradient-free revision of its natural-language skill library. We evaluate FORK on four benchmarks. Averaged over three agents on FORK-World, FORK cuts attack success rate (ASR) under adaptive attack from 78.4% to 14.1% and keeps utility above 85%, outperforming baselines on both ASR and utility. Notably, on MT-AgentRisk, whose environments and tasks are unseen in training, FORK lowers ASR from 70.6% to 9.1% with 93.1% benign utility.
